Status comes from two sources: a snapshot fetched once via getCloudSyncSwitchStatus on entry, then incremental updates from SyncObserver. The mini program\'s onFileListUpdateStatusEvent is synthesised by the container; Native has no such event channel, so the snapshot rides along with the switch query and the increments must be aggregated by hand.

Writing the switch is NOT a TTT SDK capability: the mini program calls the atop API m.wearable.sync.switch.save directly, and the SDK only offers a getter. The API is a full submit — enabled and syncType must both be sent every time.
Query switch status and sync snapshot

Status is driven by uploads only; downloads do not affect it (matching the underlying implementation) and are shown as counters. The underlying IDLE state (never synced) also maps to "Synced". Note that downloadError / downloadSuccess still mean "downloading" — only onFinish is a real end.

Audio injection is a test-only capability: it replaces microphone capture with a given audio file so the transcription / translation pipeline runs on reproducible input.\nThree constraints: (1) it only affects the phone MIC channel, not the Bluetooth earphone channel; (2) only 16kHz / mono / 16bit integer-PCM wav is supported; (3) it takes effect on the next recording only — changing it mid-recording does not affect the current one.\nThe config lives in SDK memory and is not persisted, so it is gone after a process restart.
\"%1$s\" is selected, which does not use the phone MIC channel, so these settings do not apply to it. Switch the device back to phone recording to verify injection.
Enable injection (turning it off restores real microphone capture)
Only wav files are listed, taken from the samples bundled with the demo. The SDK accepts a single file name, hence single choice. Samples are copied into place when you save.
Sent along with the injection config. The SDK does not define a range for the ANC level, so the default value 1 is always used.
Injection is off; recording uses the real microphone.
Injection mode is on: %1$s\nThe waveform and transcript come from this file, not the microphone. Tap to change.
Saved. It takes effect on the next recording

Injection is still enabled, so the next recording will use the same file. To restore real microphone capture, turn it off in Audio injection.

Runs ASR over fixed audio for several rounds, scores WER against the reference answer and exports a report.\nOne round = push injection config → start recording → wait for playback to finish → stop recording → fetch the transcript → score. A per-round timeout (audio length × 3 + 60s) covers anything that stalls; a timed-out round is marked failed and the batch continues.\nThe screen stays on while running, and leaving the page aborts the batch.

Only wav is listed, from the bundled samples in assets plus whatever you imported from a local folder; imported files win on a name clash. The reference answer is a txt with the same name as the audio (imported folder first, then assets); without it the round still runs but is not scored. Audio must be 16kHz / mono / 16bit integer PCM.

Languages and capability switches apply to every round in this batch. A batch can only use one source language, so run mixed-language material in separate batches — the cumulative CSV has a sourceLang column for cross-batch trends. These settings are not persisted; the page resets to defaults each time.

Pick wav files and their same-named txt from a local folder (such as Download); no permission is required. Remember to include the txt: a corpus imported without one still runs, it just is not scored. Imported files accumulate and survive an app restart.
This deletes every imported audio and reference file. Bundled corpora are untouched.
Not integer-PCM wav; injecting it produces no recognition at all. Convert: ffmpeg -i in.wav -ar 16000 -ac 1 -c:a pcm_s16le out.wav
